commit.message: Never review a commit that was already there

findings.title: Adoption path when priming fails has no coverage
findings.description: The `primeOk === false` branch swallows one HEAD movement, so if it ever triggers on a repository where priming merely hiccupped, the developer's commit is silently skipped — the failure mode is invisible apart from a log line. Neither new QA block exercises it: the stale-head test primes successfully and the first-commit test primes as empty.
findings.suggestion: A case that forces `headSha` to come back empty while `checkRepo` fails (for instance booting against a directory whose `.git` is unreadable, or stubbing the engine call) would pin down both that the first move is adopted rather than reviewed and that the *second* move is reviewed normally.

findings.title: Committer date can veto a genuinely new commit
findings.description: The guard fails open when the timestamp is unreadable, which is good, but a readable-yet-old committer date silently drops a real commit. `git am --committer-date-is-author-date` and `git rebase --committer-date-is-author-date` both write reflog action `commit` (so `COMMIT_ACTIONS` lets them through) while stamping an old committer date, and an explicit `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE` from tooling or a machine clock running ahead of the committing environment does the same. In those cases the extension quietly does nothing on a commit the developer just made.
findings.suggestion: Since the question is really "did this ref move just now on this machine", the reflog entry's own timestamp measures it directly and is immune to committer-date rewriting — e.g. `git reflog -1 --date=raw --format=%gd` (or the mtime of `.git/logs/HEAD`, which the watcher already tracks). Consider keying the freshness check off that instead of `%ct`.

findings.title: Stale-head test passes without any of the new code
findings.description: `makeRepo("stale-head")` creates an "init" commit, so by the time `boot()` runs, `prime()` reads a real HEAD and sets `primeOk = true` with `lastSeen` equal to the old commit. Firing the watcher with an unmoved HEAD then exits at the pre-existing `sha === this.lastSeen` guard (commit-watcher.ts:118) before reaching `primeOk` or the `FRESH_MS` check — the assertion would still pass with the entire freshness guard deleted.
findings.suggestion: Consider creating the back-dated commit *after* `boot()` rather than before, so `sha !== lastSeen`, the reflog action is `commit`, and the new committer-date check is the only thing that can suppress the review. That reproduces the wild condition the comment describes and would fail if the guard regressed.

findings.title: String.fromCharCode(10) where the adjacent line uses "\n"
findings.description: Line 106 joins the same array with `"\n"` three lines later, so the indirection reads as though it were working around something rather than being a plain newline.
findings.suggestion: Using `"\n"` here too would keep the two joins consistent.
